correctness.rationale: For every multigraph, unordered pairs of indicator events split exhaustively into union sizes four, three, two. Their numbers are C(m,2)-W+D, W-2D and D, giving the exact covariance expansion. Fixed-size coefficients are probabilities of two-three specified losses and the remaining survivors and have exactly the stated strictness ranges. Discrete convexity and a terminating simple-graph edge shift yield achievable W*=minimum with D=0 while maintaining nonisolated primaries, and positive coefficients characterize all equality cases. Independent losses substitute q^j. Exact-rational checker verified 7,132 finite multigraph profiles, all sampled survivor configurations and sample q values, but unrestricted proof does not rely on those computations.

originality.rationale: Primary full texts establish the basic coextinction model, nested-network attack tolerance, stochastic-block-ensemble robustness variance, and optimization of mean robustness, but the inspected hypotheses and conclusions do not cover the fixed-incidence two-partner model's universal variance minimum, duplicate-neighborhood correction, or exact boundary equality classes. A general unindexed induced-edge variance theorem is a material residual risk.
residual_risks: An earlier graph-theoretic sampled-induced-edge variance minimization result may be unindexed or use unexpected terminology; if it supplies the same equality classes, originality would need reassessment.

value.rationale: At given n,m and loss level every allowed interaction network has exactly the same mean number of secondary extinctions, so variance is a natural independent uncertainty measure. The theorem gives a global and simultaneously sharp minimum under both natural extinction sampling regimes, splits preventable uncertainty into primary degree heterogeneity and duplicated partner-neighborhood components, and completely classifies interior and boundary equality cases. A connected six-primary example yields a variance ratio of 26/15 at q=1/2 with identical mean; useful as a quantitative null benchmark for comparing two-partner ecological networks. Results do not purport to predict real ecological rescue dynamics.
